diagrams.title: Context Diagram (DFD level 0)

data.name: Weather API
data.reasonOutOfScope: External third-party service (openweathermap.org). We do not control or own this system. Only the data flows to/from it are in scope for threat modeling.

data.name: Park Open Source Data
data.reasonOutOfScope: External open data source (OpenStreetMap / Overpass API). Publicly accessible, read-only. We do not control this system, only our consumption of it is in scope.

data.name: Instagram data
data.description: Android OS usage stats for Instagram
data.reasonOutOfScope: Provided by the Android OS (UsageStatsManager). We do not control Instagram or the Android OS internals, only how our app reads and processes this data is in scope.

data.name: No-as-a-service
data.reasonOutOfScope: External third-party API. We do not control or own this service. Only the data flow from this API into our app is in scope.

data.name: Android Local Calendar
data.reasonOutOfScope: External service (calendar.google.com). We do not control Google's infrastructure. Only how our app requests and handles calendar event data is in scope.

data.name: Android App Usage Stats
data.reasonOutOfScope: Provided by the Android OS (UsageStatsManager API). We do not control the Android operating system, only how our app requests and stores usage data is in scope.

data.name: BAYG? App
data.description: Android application, Bestie, are you good?

data.name: CBS StatLine
data.reasonOutOfScope: External government open data service (opendata.cbs.nl). We do not control CBS's infrastructure or the accuracy of their published statistics. Only how our app fetches and displays the Dutch national average data is in scope.

diagrams.description: Context Diagram to provide an overview of our app BAYG.

threats.title: Password exposed in network traffic
threats.description: If HTTPS is not enforced, credentials can be intercepted
threats.mitigation: Enforce HTTPS; use Android `NetworkSecurityConfig` to block cleartext

threats.title: Weak hash algorithm used (MD5/SHA1)
threats.description: Dev uses wrong algorithm, hash is easily cracked
threats.mitigation: Enforce Argon2id in code; document in code review checklist

threats.title: Biometric data stored outside secure hardware
threats.description: Raw biometric data should NEVER leave the TEE
threats.mitigation: Use Android `BiometricPrompt` API only, never store biometric data yourself

threats.title: Session token stored unencrypted
threats.description: Token in plaintext SharedPreferences, readable via ADB

data.name: Show dashboard
data.description: Aggregates all data, displays to user

data.name: Stats Database
data.description: Stores: crashout events, usage history, streaks

data.name: Password Auth
data.description: Verifies password using Argon2id hash comparison

threats.title: Attacker impersonates user with stolen hash
threats.description: If hash is extracted, attacker cracks it offline
threats.mitigation: Argon2id with high cost factor makes cracking infeasible

threats.title: Auth bypass via Frida hook
threats.description: Attacker hooks auth function to return "success"
threats.mitigation: Use CryptoObject, auth result is cryptographic, not just a boolean

data.name: Users Database
data.description: Stores: email, Argon2id hash, salt, session token.

threats.title: Hash stored without salt
threats.description: Without salt, rainbow tables crack hashes instantly
threats.mitigation: Always generate unique salt per user with "SecureRandom"

threats.title: Database extracted via ADB backup
threats.description: `adb backup` exposes full DB on non-rooted device
